name: Kaisanic
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: van Dam, Kellen Parker & Nora Muheim. 2023. A first description of Kaisan, a Tibeto-Burman language of Myanmar. Paper, 26th Himalayan Languages Symposium, Paris. 22pp.
earlier_scan.note: First description (22pp, 2023) plausibly covers prosody/stress; conference paper not found online.

sources.citation: HLS26 program, 26th Himalayan Languages Symposium, Paris 2023.
sources.note: Only lists the talk (Parker van Dam, Kellen and Nora Mulheim [sic], 4 Sept 14h00). No content.

sources.citation: University of Helsinki Research Portal, activity record: van Dam, Kellen Parker & Nora Josefina Muheim, 'A first description of Kaisan, a North Patkaian language on Myanmar', oral presentation, 4 Sept 2023, HLS26 Paris (same abstract text).
sources.note: Same abstract; tonal (4 tones), 'iambic compounds'; no stress statement. Lists the only prior Kaisan resource: Rauh 2017 Kahgahmyond (community dictionary).

sources.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker & Nora Muheim. 2023. A first description of Kaisan, a North Patkaian language of Myanmar. Abstract, in: Booklet of abstracts, 26th Himalayan Languages Symposium, INALCO, Paris, 4-6 Sept 2023, p. 62 (booklet lists van Dam alone, Univ. of Zurich; program and Helsinki portal list van Dam & Muheim).
sources.note: Abstract only (the 22-pp paper itself is not online). Says Kaisan has 'a clear four-way phonemic tonal distinction with secondary features of duration and phonation, a lack of significant tone or vowel neutralisation as seen elsewhere in Northern Naga within iambic compounds'; nothing on word stress placement.

sources.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker. 2022. Tangsa-Nocte as a Continuum: A diagnostic feature list for classification of varieties. Himalayan Linguistics. doi:10.5070/h920253557
sources.note: No mention of Kaisan; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Morey, Stephen. 2019. The Tangsa-Nocte languages: An introduction. Himalayan Linguistics 18(1). doi:10.5070/h918142626
sources.note: No mention of Kaisan; discusses the Haimi/Heimi vs Rangpang grouping (the group Kaisan is assigned to). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker. 2018. The tone system of Tangsa-Nocte and related northern Naga varieties. PhD thesis, La Trobe University. 333 pp. doi:10.26181/21858474.v1
sources.note: Kaisan is named once (p. 99) as a Tangwa (non-Rangpang) Tangsa variety 'not discussed here'; no Kaisan data. General Tangsa-Nocte remarks only: sesquisyllabic presyllables/prefixes are 'toneless and unstressed'; emphasis is realised 'through lengthening and stress'. Not a Kaisan stress statement.

sources.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker & Nora Muheim. 2023. A first description of Kaisan, a Tibeto-Burman language of Myanmar. Paper, 26th Himalayan Languages Symposium, Paris, 4-6 Sept 2023. 22 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only description of Kaisan; the abstract promises 'phonology and tone' and discusses iambic compounds, so the paper is where any stress/prosody statement would be. Glottolog (ref 674776) holds a copy (eurasia/) in Hammarström's private bibliography; not online. Ask the authors (nora.muheim@helsinki.fi; van Dam, Univ. Passau / La Trobe).
